newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy Chamber approves three-year economic plan.
newsitem.headline: Italy Chamber approves three-year economic plan.

text.p: Italy's Chamber of Deputies (lower house) on Friday approved the centre-left government's three-year programme of key economic targets.

The plan, known as the DPEF, now passes to the Senate (upper house), where a vote is expected on Tuesday. The programme sets strict targets for 1998-2000 to keep Italy on track to join Europe's planned economic and monetary union at its 1999 launch.

The Communist Refoundation party, whose support ensures Prime Minister Romano Prodi's majority, voted in favour of the document, which passed by 282 votes to 158. It said it planned to abstain in the Senate, where its support is not vital.

The DPEF targets an ambitious 1998 deficit-to-Gross Domestic Product ratio of 2.8 percent after planned deficit cuts of 25 trillion lire ($15 billion). The ratio is below the important three percent threshold set for aspiring EMU members.

Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said in an interview this week that Italy, which is desperate to join EMU at the outset, would send a convergence plan mapping out how it intends to keep its finances straight to Brussels by the weekend.

The DPEF forecast 2.0 percent GDP growth next year and a 1.8 percent rise in inflation. It also called for restructuring of the welfare state, the details of which are now being negotiated by labour unions, employers, trade bodies and the government.
